samples.summary: Unrelated feature bundled with the #1045 undo work: share-link live revalidation + readOnly remount.
samples.evidence: The originating plan (docs/tasks/active/20260907-docs-select-all-type-undo-todo.md) scopes this change to `withUndoUnit`, `deleteSelection`, composite handlers, the Yorkie undo floor, one test file and one design-doc section. The diff additionally rewrites `SharedDocumentByToken` to poll `resolveShareLink` every 60 s (`SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS`), adds `readOnly` to the mount effects of docs/notes/slides views (forcing an editor+store rebuild mid-session), adds `YorkieDocStore.dispose()`, and re-checks `readOnly`/`disposed`/`pasting` in `pastePlainTextFromClipboard`. None of that is undo granularity; it is a separate permission-enforcement feature with its own product and load implications, riding in an undo-fix PR.

samples.summary: Share-link authority model changed (one-shot resolve → periodic revalidation + mid-session editor rebuild) with no update to docs/design/sharing.md.
samples.evidence: sharing.md still documents the route as "Resolves the token, sets up YorkieProvider…" and describes client-side `readOnly` as the effective write boundary, with revocation only "immediately invalidating the token" for new resolutions. The new behaviour — a 60 s refetch interval, refetch on focus, eviction of the view after two failed resolves, and rebuilding the docs/notes/slides editors when the role downgrades — is an architecture-level change to that model and is recorded only in code comments and in docs-collaboration.md (a docs-editor doc, not the sharing doc). CONTRIBUTING expects the canonical subsystem doc to be updated.

samples.summary: A transient REST-API failure now tears down an open shared editing session ("Link unavailable"), discarding editor state.
samples.evidence: With `retry: 1` and `refetchInterval: 60_000`, two consecutive failed `resolveShareLink` calls make `error` truthy and the component renders the "Link unavailable" screen in place of the whole document view, unmounting the editor. The REST API and the Yorkie sync server are separate dependencies (see docs/design/sync-status.md, which treats offline/unsynced editing as a supported state), so an API-only outage or a laptop sleeping through two intervals can evict a session whose local edits may not yet be synced. The comment's justification ("a document that cannot reach the API is not syncing either") conflates the two services. Failing closed on a *revoked* link is the goal; failing closed on a network blip is a user-visible data-risk behaviour that the design docs do not sanction.

samples.summary: Applying a permission change by rebuilding the editor+store discards session state, including the undo history this PR is about.
samples.evidence: Adding `readOnly` to the mount effect deps recreates `YorkieDocStore` and re-runs `initialize()`. `YorkieDocStore`'s constructor calls `markUndoFloor()` at the current stack top, so after any readOnly flip (notably a viewer→editor upgrade, which the new polling makes reachable) every pre-existing undo entry sits at or below the new floor and `canUndo()` refuses it — the user's whole undo history for the session is gone, plus caret/scroll/find state. Threading `readOnly` into the already-mounted editor (as `setTheme`/`setViewMode` are threaded) is the layer that avoids this; remount is the blunt instrument.

samples.summary: Notes gains the same remount-on-readOnly path but not the store teardown docs added, so each rebuild leaks a live doc subscription.
samples.evidence: `docs-view.tsx` cleanup now calls `store.dispose()` precisely because the Yorkie document outlives the store; `slides-view.tsx` already calls `store.dispose()`. `notes-view.tsx`'s cleanup still only nulls `storeRef`, and `YorkieNoteStore`'s constructor (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:143) registers `doc.subscribe(...)` with no unsubscribe and the class has no `dispose()`. The new remount trigger makes that leak reachable on every permission flip; the pattern is applied inconsistently across the three views the same commit touches.

samples.summary: The depth-based undo floor bug is fixed in YorkieDocStore only; YorkieNoteStore keeps the identical `undoFloor = stack.length` pattern.
samples.evidence: `YorkieDocStore` now holds the floor by entry identity (`undoFloorMark`) because Yorkie's 50-entry cap shifts entries off the bottom and makes a recorded depth lie. `YorkieNoteStore` does `this.undoFloor = doc.getUndoStackForTest().length` and presumably compares lengths in `canUndo()`, so the same class of stranded-undo bug remains there, and the two collaborative stores now answer the same question differently. Either fix both or record in the design doc why notes is exempt.

samples.summary: The "one user action, one undo unit" goal is met only for keyboard/clipboard paths; toolbar block ops and Replace All still lose data on large selections.
samples.evidence: The new doc section states that `toggleList` / `indent` / `outdent` / `applyBlockStyle`, the cell-range style loop and `FindReplaceState.replaceAll()` still issue one unbatched write per block (two per match), "so on a selection larger than the 50-entry cap they lose their oldest writes exactly as the keyboard paths did before #1045". The issue's goal is "One user action = one undo unit for every selection-replacing edit"; Replace All over a large document is the same unrecoverable-data shape and remains shippable-broken, deferred to issue #1048. Deliberate and documented, hence minor, but worth weighing before promotion since the fix is the same two-line `doc.batch(...)`.

samples.summary: `MemDocStore.batch()` no longer "mirrors `MemSlidesStore.batch()`" — the two in-memory undo models have diverged.
samples.evidence: The retained comment claims parity with `MemSlidesStore.batch()`, but that store (packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:1789) still unconditionally pushes a checkpoint and clears redo inside `batch()`, with no `willWrite()`/adoption logic. After this change the two stores answer the `snapshot(); batch(…)` and empty-batch-redo questions differently; the cross-reference is now misleading for the next person keeping them in step.

finding.summary: A transient REST-API failure now tears down an open shared editing session ("Link unavailable"), discarding editor state.
finding.evidence: With `retry: 1` and `refetchInterval: 60_000`, two consecutive failed `resolveShareLink` calls make `error` truthy and the component renders the "Link unavailable" screen in place of the whole document view, unmounting the editor. The REST API and the Yorkie sync server are separate dependencies (see docs/design/sync-status.md, which treats offline/unsynced editing as a supported state), so an API-only outage or a laptop sleeping through two intervals can evict a session whose local edits may not yet be synced. The comment's justification ("a document that cannot reach the API is not syncing either") conflates the two services. Failing closed on a *revoked* link is the goal; failing closed on a network blip is a user-visible data-risk behaviour that the design docs do not sanction.

verdict.reason: Verified in the working tree. shared-document.tsx:1107-1119 configures the resolve query with retry:1 + refetchInterval 60s + refetchOnWindowFocus, and lines 1125-1137 render the "Link unavailable" screen on `error` even though `resolved` retains the last successful value — replacing SharedDocumentInner (line 1139) and unmounting the YorkieProvider/CollabDocumentProvider and editor. resolveShareLink (api/share-links.ts:99-111) is a plain fetch+assertOk that throws on any 5xx/network failure, and App.tsx:88 uses a bare `new QueryClient()` with no defaultOptions or placeholderData, so nothing suppresses or downgrades that error state; there is no branch distinguishing a 404/410 revoked/expired link from a transient API failure. Yorkie sync uses a separate RPC endpoint (line 1006), so the in-code justification at lines 1104-1106 does conflate two independent dependencies. The repo's own docs treat this state as protected: sync-status.md:29-38 makes "closing a tab that holds unpushed edits requires a deliberate confirmation" a Goal, lines 42-49 confirm no offline persistence (no Yorkie `store` passed), and shared-header-status.tsx:8-12 states an editor-role share visitor "can strand work exactly like an owned editor can". A route-level unmount discards those unpushed edits with no confirmation and bypasses the beforeunload guard. No guard or caller elsewhere makes this unreachable, so I cannot refute on any named ground; the impact (user-visible loss of unsynced edits on an API-only outage) keeps it blocking under this lens's impact-based severity rule.

searchedFor: grep readOnly in slides-view.tsx, notes-view.tsx, board-view.tsx, sheet-view.tsx
finding.summary: Revalidation only tightens authority for docs/sheets/board; slides and notes still capture `readOnly` once, so an editor→viewer downgrade never reaches them
finding.evidence: `SharedDocumentByToken` now re-resolves the token every 60s and pushes the fresh `role` down (`shared-document.tsx:1089-1120`), and each layout derives `readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"` (`shared-document.tsx:330, 383, 433, 460`). Only `docs-view.tsx` (this delta), `board-view.tsx:851` and `sheet-view.tsx:1341` list `readOnly` in the mount-effect deps. `slides-view.tsx:1222-1228` explicitly excludes it — "it is derived from a share-link role that is fixed for the lifetime of the route, so toggling it at runtime is not a supported scenario" — and `notes-view.tsx:157` also mounts on `[didMount, doc]` only. This delta invalidates exactly that assumption without updating either view, so on a slides or notes share link a downgraded visitor keeps a fully writable editor, and with the default `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` unset (docs/design/sharing.md:200-219) the client gate is the real write boundary. The stated outcome — bounding how long a downgraded link keeps its authority — is therefore met for only part of the shared surface, and the now-false comment in slides-view will mislead the next reader.

verdict.reason: The finding's core factual claim is contradicted by the code. It asserts slides-view.tsx excludes `readOnly` from the mount-effect deps with a comment saying the share-link role "is fixed for the lifetime of the route, so toggling it at runtime is not a supported scenario" — but slides-view.tsx:1237 has deps `[didMount, doc, readOnlyMount]` (with `readOnlyMount = readOnly === true` at :198), and the comment at :1226-1235 states the opposite: "`readOnlyMount` IS listed, and is load-bearing… A share-link role is no longer fixed for the route's lifetime — the `/shared/:token` view re-resolves its token on an interval (`SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS`)… Listing it rebuilds the editor against the current permission." The quoted text is absent from the file. The second claimed location is equally wrong: notes-view.tsx:167 has deps `[didMount, doc, readOnly]`, and :156-165 carries the same updated rationale citing `SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS` and the editor→viewer mid-session downgrade. The upstream plumbing the finding describes is real (shared-document.tsx:1107-1119 refetchInterval; :384/:434/:461 derive `readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"`; :418 and :470/473 forward it into NotesView/SlidesView), but that plumbing plus the listed deps means a downgrade DOES re-mount both editors against the new permission. The asserted unmet-acceptance consequence — a downgraded visitor keeping a fully writable deck or note — cannot arise by the described mechanism, and no stale comment remains to mislead.
